correctness.rationale: For the literal four-symbol fixed point, odd shifts are impossible by position parity. The binary coding recurrence is proved from the substitution and identifies the published Rudin–Shapiro word, yielding the cardinality lower bound by Theorem 28. All infinite length-67 factors equal a computationally saturated 528-word language: substitution powers 11 and 12 have identical factor sets, and the finite-language operator is closed. Exact bitset operations on this complete language prove coverage of shifts 2,4,6,8,10, and its forcing witnesses, and exhaustively find exactly two successful 4-subsets among all 40920 candidate even 4-subsets up to 66, none below 66. A standalone standard-library verifier recomputes every certificate and independently checks a long prefix. Finite testing is not used as a substitute for the saturation lemma.

value.rationale: Pseudoperiods are natural fixed finite sets of forward-return probes; both the shortest return horizon and fewest probes are explicit optimization questions from the primary literature. For the canonical four-state Rudin–Shapiro substitution the best-delay solution requires five shifts, while the sparsest solution uses four shifts at a much larger 66 horizon, and there are exactly two minimum-delay sparse solutions. This complete sharp tradeoff is a structural infinite-word result, beyond a routine arithmetic restatement or finite-prefix numerical sample.
